findings.pass_item: 3 (a surviving mutant is a finding); 1 (REQ-111 criterion 12: «in every state of the demo that the test reaches ... the text that the page shows»)
findings.place: app/test/e2e/landing.test.js: LD-5 section B (readState «after Назад» and «after Назад to 1»), LD-6 (readState `${where} result`), also the result states of LD-5, LD-7, LD-8 and LD-9; app/test/fixtures/e2e-kit.js readState
findings.what: The lint of the shown text never sees the live line that the demo writes after the result and after «Назад». demo.js writes it 30 ms after the action (ANNOUNCE_MS), and the tests read `document.body.innerText` before that: in LD-6 a debug read of #live right before readState printed an empty string for all 7 fixtures and the no-match pass in ru and kk. Mutants: M-F51 `announce(fill(t("live_result"), { kind: first.name + " 5 минут" }))` stays green under LD-5, LD-6, LD-7, LD-8 and LD-9 (each run alone); M-F47 and M-F52 (a price or guarantee word added to the live_back announcement) stay green under LD-5. The same word added to the live_answer announcement is red in LD-5 (M-F50, the next heading comes later than 30 ms), so the check works where the test waits and is blind where it does not. The design's section 10 says a page script that writes a list form only after a tap (M88) is red in LD-5 or LD-6 «into the live line»; for the result and Back announcements it is not. The words of these two announcements are texts of the texts module (linted by check-public in all languages) and a solution name (linted in the intake), so only a literal written by a script reaches the screen unlinted, which is exactly the case the criterion names («so a text that a page script writes is linted as well»).
findings.needed: Before each readState that follows a result or a «Назад», wait until the live line holds its announcement (`page.waitForFunction(() => document.getElementById("live")?.textContent !== "")`, or a wait of more than ANNOUNCE_MS plus a frame) and assert its text equals the filled value of live_result (with the solution's name) or live_back (with the number) in the page's language; do the same in the public set's result states of LD-9. Show M-F51 red under LD-6 and LD-9 and M-F47/F52 red under LD-5, and the code green.
findings.goes_to: TEST-DESIGNER (tests only; the code is right: the announce delay is the design's)

findings.place: app/test/unit/office-view.test.js OV-3; app/public/office/view.js onFrame (the line `if (deps.hidden()) return;` inside the frame)
findings.what: Mutant D26 (that line removed) stays green. OV-3 hides the page through a visibility event that cancels the frame that was asked for, so the frame callback never runs while hidden. The guard inside the callback (a callback that runs after the flag turned and before the event) has no test; ask() keeps its own guard and D27 (it removed) is red in OV-3. Browsers do not run such callbacks in a hidden tab, so the criterion («while the page is hidden no frame is requested or drawn») holds either way; this is a defence in depth with no test.
findings.needed: In OV-3 set the hidden flag without firing the visibility event, run the pending frame callback, and assert no frame is drawn and none is asked for.

findings.place: app/test/unit/office-view.test.js (OV-2, OV-4) and office-stage.test.js OS-7; app/public/office/view.js STEP_FRAME_MS
findings.what: Mutant I23 (STEP_FRAME_MS 160 to 100 in view.js) stays green. OS-7 proves that createWalker changes its step frame every frameMs it is given (160 in the test), and no test reads the value that view.js gives it, so the walking animation's frame time of the view is unmeasured. No criterion states the 160 ms; the design (4.6) and the look do.
findings.needed: In OV-2 read the `frame` of the figure that the recording context sees (or the walker's position().frame) at two times 160 ms apart during a walk and assert it alternates, or state in the design that the value is a look detail with no test.
findings.goes_to: TEST-DESIGNER or ORCH (a decision to accept)
